item.title: Googly-eyed buoys and kites help keep seabirds out of fishing nets, study finds
item.description: Off the coast of Cornwall in southwest England, a pole rises from a buoy with a pair of big eyes on top. The head spins, creating what researchers call an “animated eye effect.” Its job is to scare away seabirds away before they dive into the fishing net below. On other nets, a kite shaped […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Mother bats' hearts beat faster at the sound of their own babies' cries
item.description: A mother bat has one crucial challenge: find her own babies among hundreds of other bats in the colony. Making sure she cares for and nurses only her own offspring is important to ensuring their survival. Among Japanese house bats, mothers keep track of their pups using the babies' isolation calls. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El Niño Then and Now
item.description: A 35-year satellite altimetry record lets scientists hold this year’s El Niño up against its strongest predecessors. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: 40 years later, Chernobyl's nuclear fallout is not what scientists expected
item.description: Forty years after the Chornobyl disaster, tiny radioactive particles still linger in the soil, carrying a dangerous legacy. Using powerful X-rays, scientists discovered that some of these particles have remained surprisingly stable, trapping radioactive substances inside instead of releasing them into the environment. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How we mark our ballot can affect how we feel about voting. Here's why
item.description: Have you ever left a polling place feeling that your mark on the ballot didn't quite say what you wanted it to? Perhaps you liked two candidates but had to drop one, or backed the one who might actually win over the one you preferred. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
item.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: About six years ago, hearing researcher Dr. Kelly Miles had a stroke just a week after having a baby. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
item.description: Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How Zimbabwe's government turned international condemnation into political ammunition
item.description: International pressure intended to encourage democratic reform can sometimes strengthen the very governments it seeks to hold to account, according to new research from The University of Manchester. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese astronomers find real 3-body system. It is not what Liu Cixin thinks
item.description: In author and computer engineer Liu Cixin’s science fiction hit The Three-Body Problem, three suns throw a doomed world into chaos. Chinese astronomers say they have found a real three-star system that is far better behaved. Using FAST, the world’s biggest single-dish radio telescope in southwestern China, the researchers found two dead stars and a “living” one locked in a steady cosmic dance about 7,000 light years from Earth. One of the dead stars is a pulsar that spins more than 300 times a... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: New test measures potentially harmful metals in cellulose food packaging
item.description: A technique for detecting potentially harmful metals in regenerated cellulose food packaging is discussed in the International Journal of Environment and Pollution. The new tool can be used for safety assessments of materials increasingly used as alternatives to conventional plastics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
item.description: MIT researchers marooned 13 AIs on a virtual island, and they responded by inventing games, mourning a lost ring and, eventually, getting better at their jobs. Fuente: TechCrunch.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Mehta

item.title: Autonomous triangular modules could build tomorrow's mega-observatories
item.description: Private companies are getting better at launching more mass into space with larger rockets. But there is still a major constraint on the size of objects we can get into orbit—fairing size. This places physical constraints on the overall shape of what we can launch and severely limits the sizes of, say, a communications array or a power satellite. But a new paper from researchers at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and the Beijing Institute of Technology offers a solution—a self-shaping, deployable module that can fine-tune both its positioning and its own dimensions. The… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a hidden immune weapon against deadly lung cancer
item.description: Researchers have uncovered a hidden immune defense capable of attacking small cell lung cancer, an extremely aggressive disease that often escapes conventional treatments. The specialized immune cells can recognize and destroy cancer cells even when tumors have disguised themselves from the immune system. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Researchers develop AI tool to map microRNA binding sites on circular RNAs
item.description: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are loop-shaped molecules that can influence gene regulation through interactions with microRNAs (miRNAs). This matters because circRNAs can exist as different full-length isoforms, and their back-splice junction (BSJ) connects the two ends of the RNA. Treating a circular RNA like a linear transcript can therefore overlook sequence information near this junction. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Acupuncture and mutual exchange in Chinese and Soviet science
item.description: Previous accounts of the scientific relationship between communist China and the Soviet Union have depicted it as one of subordination, with the Russians exporting knowledge to the Chinese or scavenging from their bodies of knowledge. A new article in Isis, however, posits that the relationship between Chinese and Soviet scientists was instead one of mutual exchange. In "Brief Encounter: Acupuncture, Pavlov, and Scientific Exchange Between China and the Soviet Union, 1949-1961," authors Liang Wan, Simon Huxtable and Sarah Marks explore the role of acupuncture in uniting the Pavlovian science… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Light-activated catalyst makes sustainable production of hydrogen peroxide more efficient
item.description: Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) is a versatile chemical feedstock whose industrial production relies predominantly on an energy-intensive process with a substantial environmental footprint. One alternative is to produce it using a catalyst activated by light. In an international research project involving the Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces, researchers have now developed a synthesis strategy that allows them to precisely control the spatial arrangement of ions in a carbon nitride. The resulting photocatalyst is three times as efficient as conventional green production methods. The… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Material substitution can increase the potential environmental impact of packaging systems
item.description: New research suggests that replacing polyethylene (PE) packaging with paper, glass, aluminum or steel often does not reduce environmental impacts across a product's life cycle. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What is a neutrino anyway? A look at the science behind this year's Nobel Prize in Physics
item.description: If you wanted a Nobel Prize, you would do well to study neutrinos. To date, the Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded five times to research related to neutrino detection and discovery. This year, Francis Halzen earned the Nobel "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Revamped playground design could protect children around the world from dangers of the sun
item.description: A new design methodology for school playgrounds is demonstrating how children can still enjoy their playtime while being protected from the harmful effects of the sun. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ultrafast light pulses track molecular motion with three-femtosecond resolution
item.description: Researchers have observed a molecule in the first instants after it has absorbed light and tracked the coordinated motion of electrons and nuclei with a temporal resolution of three femtoseconds. This is the result achieved by an international research group led by the Politecnico di Milano, which has developed a new apparatus for studying ultrafast photochemical processes. Fuente: Phys.org.

Katmai's salmon runs are one of the few places that many brown bears tolerate eac... Ver más metapodcast Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Shrinking iron films strengthens laser-driven demagnetization
item.description: From photos and videos to documents, vast amounts of data are stored on hard drives in large data centers. These devices use tiny magnetic regions whose orientation determines the information stored. But how could data be stored even faster in the future? One possible approach involves ultrashort laser pulses, which can alter the magnetic order of materials in an extremely short time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researcher tackles impact of a CMO's life events on businesses' bottom line
item.description: When a major company's CEO goes through a messy divorce or is arrested for drunk driving, investors often get nervous, worried that the executive's personal struggles will dent their returns. But most people hardly notice when a chief marketing officer has similar personal problems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global database provides a fuller picture of the elements that make up plant life
item.description: What, exactly, is a plant made of? Scientists have a good understanding of the essential nutrients plants need to grow. But what plants need and what they contain are not necessarily the same. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Supramolecular assembly opens a new route to building quantum materials
item.description: A joint research team fabricated a two-dimensional structure that exhibits properties of both the honeycomb and Kagome lattices using organic molecules. They discovered that edge states specific to topological materials (states that exist only at the edges and are distinct from those in the interior) appear in this structure. The team included researchers from NIMS, Toyota Kosen (National Institute of Technology, Toyota College), Saga University, Nara Women's University, Kiel University (Germany) and other institutions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Helping microgreens pack even more of a nutritional punch
item.description: Microgreens are nutritional powerhouses. A team of plant scientists at Penn State conducting research on multiple aspects of microgreens recently published three studies reporting progress on multiple fronts, including iron enrichment, productive indoor growth and a faux lightning technique that could improve microgreens' growth, yield and nutritional quality. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Amino acid stabilizes material's quantum state above room temperature
item.description: New research started with a special material that behaves unusually when it's extremely cold—135 degrees below zero Fahrenheit (minus 93 degrees Celsius), close to the most frigid temperature ever recorded in Antarctica—and showed that the unusual behavior could be extended to well above room temperature—up to about 135 F (57 degrees Celsius), close to the highest heat ever measured in Death Valley, California. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Invites Media to 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium
item.description: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s symposium is focused on humanity’s return to the Moon, sustainable lunar infrastructure, advanced space propulsion, and the evolving space workforce. Panels […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Lee Mohon

item.title: DNA and underwater footage reveal two new species of deep-sea siphonophores
item.description: New research is shedding light on the diversity of deep-sea siphonophores. A team of scientists from MBARI, the University of Gdańsk, New York University and Yale University conducted a comprehensive examination of Bargmannia siphonophores using museum material, submersible observations and genomic sequencing. This work uncovered two previously unknown species: Bargmannia marlena and Bargmannia pyrosa. The team published their findings in the Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society last week. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Canine cancer patients contribute to next-generation minimally invasive cancer therapies for dogs and humans
item.description: Natural disasters. Hikes. Long, dark nights alone. For many people, dogs offer a sense of safety and comfort in challenging or uncertain times. Cancer researchers at a new lab at Purdue University are partnering with dogs to make cancer less frightening—and less deadly—to some of humanity's very best friends using a technique called tumor ablation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Natural forest regeneration helps curb spread of invasive species
item.description: The presence of non-native trees is often seen as an obstacle to the recovery of tropical forests regrowing in previously deforested areas. To better understand the behavior of these plants over time in both humid and dry forests, researchers from approximately 60 institutions analyzed data from over 1,500 areas of forest regeneration across the Americas. The results, published in the journal Nature Plants, indicate that the initial dominance of exotic species is temporary. They multiply easily during the first 10 to 20 years, taking advantage of abundant sunlight in open areas. However, they… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The assumption about farm automation that may be wrong
item.description: You've likely heard this assumption: When AI-enabled and autonomous machines arrive on the farm, jobs will disappear. But researchers at the University of California, Davis, who studied 16 fruit tree operations in California and Washington for three years, found that automation still takes human knowledge. What changes is how the work gets done. The study, drawing on 165 in-depth interviews with workers and growers, was published in the journal New Technology, Work and Employment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Public health programs can 'rewire' social networks, study finds
item.description: An educational program intended to improve maternal and child health fundamentally altered the social fabric of the rural Honduran villages where it was implemented, a new Yale-led study finds. The findings, researchers say, have implications for interventions anywhere that seek to improve people's well-being by disseminating information or changing behaviors through social contagion. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Disiplinang walang palo: Challenging common Filipino parenting misbeliefs
item.description: More frequent spanking is linked to greater anxiety and aggression in children over time, according to international research that includes Filipino families presented by psychology professor Dr. Liane Peña Alampay of the Ateneo de Manila University. The findings challenge the familiar belief that "pamamalo" produces more disciplined children, pointing instead to the benefits of warm relationships in the home, clear expectations and nonviolent disciplining. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stream restoration improves biodiversity but not necessarily ecosystem functioning
item.description: The EU Nature Restoration Regulation adopted in 2024 establishes the restoration of ecosystem functions as an objective of stream restoration. But can conventional measures that focus primarily on restoring the physical structure of rivers and streams fulfill this task? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study: Pandemic arrest patterns may have deepened existing inequalities in policing
item.description: The COVID-19 pandemic was a public health crisis that affected more than the public's health. It brought complex changes across many aspects of society, including having an influence on suburban arrest patterns, according to a study co-authored by University at Buffalo researchers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ants break a basic rule of biology to help them adapt to new environments
item.description: A new study led by researchers in the Eco-Evo-Devo lab at the University of Ottawa finds that ants can decouple antenna size from both head and body size as they develop into different social castes, revealing how social signals and hormones help shape traits for specialized colony roles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: After 2005 rat removal, three seabird species on a Pacific island grew up to tenfold over decades
item.description: The successful eradication of invasive rodents in 2005 has greatly influenced seabird populations on Surprise Island. Researchers closely monitored seven seabird species to document their recovery post-eradication. While some species thrived quickly, others needed more extended observation to show signs of improvement. Notably, noddies saw a significant increase in breeding pairs, whereas red-footed boobies showed a more gradual recovery. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Meta turns Muse sharing back on
item.description: Meta has re-enabled Muse sharing after security researchers had reported that public conversation links could be easy to find. The researchers said they had been able to find Muse pages like a marketing company's internal revenue review and a small business owner's loan application. Researchers at Claroc reported earlier this week that Muse the web […] Fuente: The Verge.
item.dc:creator: Jay Peters

item.title: Microplastics in sediment could trace decades of human activity worldwide
item.description: In a review article recently published in the journal Earth-Science Reviews, researchers from the Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde (IOW), in collaboration with colleagues from the University of Leicester (United Kingdom), report on how human activity has altered Earth's sediments over the decades. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A house ages alongside its occupants, according to researcher
item.description: Flemish people are very attached to their homes and generally wish to stay there for as long as possible. However, many homes were not designed to be lived in for a lifetime. Architect and researcher Sander Lambrix has analyzed the relationship between our homes and our well-being as we grow older. His conclusion: a home is much more than just a physical environment, whether or not it is suited to an aging body. People and their homes are deeply connected on an emotional level. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study highlights need for policymakers to look at digital policies as part of energy, climate planning
item.description: A new study underscores the extent to which digital policies cannot be separated from energy policies. The research evaluates the relationship between information communication technologies and carbon dioxide emissions and finds that the variables the researchers used as proxies for digitalization were associated with increased emissions. The paper, "ICT and CO₂ Emissions in the G20: A Channel-Based Mediation Analysis," is published in the journal Sustainability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A parasite carried by one-third of humanity can't reproduce if one key protein is disabled
item.description: A protein discovered in a Virginia Tech–led study may open a gateway to treatments for a parasite responsible for a deadly disease in immunocompromised people. The team led by Raj Gaji, assistant professor of parasitology at the Virginia-Maryland College of Veterinary Medicine working in the Center for One Health Research, identified a protein the team named DDP that helps Toxoplasma gondii build its offspring. When researchers switched it off, the parasites stopped multiplying entirely. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Clustering changes how charged polymers separate in water, challenging old assumptions
item.description: A polymer science revelation about how liquid mixtures separate could have major implications for human health, metabolism and disease, new research indicates. In a brief report published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME) Professor Matthew Tirrell and Freie Universität Berlin Professor Matthias Ballauff revealed previously overlooked factors at play in the separation of charged polyelectrolyte polymers in water, challenging assumptions that have dominated the field since the 1950s. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chiricahua is the nation's newest national park—what does that mean?
item.description: With a stroke of a pen, President Donald Trump has officially created the United States' 64th national park. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: More than 20 years of data challenge one-size-fits-all view of Arctic cloud-forming particles
item.description: As the climate gets warmer, the number of particles that make up clouds in the Arctic may increase or decrease, depending on the specific area. A new study indicates that the Arctic should be divided into three parts rather than considered as a whole. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: We must prepare entire cities for extreme heat. Our new study reveals how
item.description: In Australia, the days are growing longer and summer is fast approaching. But a very strong El Niño—a natural weather phenomenon that drives variations in temperature and winds across the Pacific—could make this summer a sweltering one. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The psychology that can lead investors to make bad financial decisions
item.description: Say you buy shares in a company. The price climbs and months later you sell for a healthy profit. Ask why it worked, and the answer is often some version of "I made a good call." Now imagine the trade had lost money instead. Would you be as quick to blame your own judgment? Many of us wouldn't. We may point to bad timing, a jittery market, anything but ourselves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nontoxic 'light-activated' compound shows promise for safer 3D printing of advanced biomaterials
item.description: Scientists from Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) have developed a new class of light-activated compounds that could lead to safer and more versatile applications in 3D printing, cosmetics and medicine. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
item.description: Searches for Samsung foldables just happened to skyrocket following iPhone Duo unveiling. Fuente: Ars Technica.

item.title: Access to ASL from birth increases childhood math proficiency in deaf children
item.description: One fish. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The dark side of the energy transition: Renewable megaprojects may sacrifice local communities' rights
item.description: An international study involving ICTA-UAB reveals that large energy corporations use corporate sustainability narratives to legitimize wind, solar and hydropower projects that, in practice, exclude communities from fair economic and financial returns and ignore the projects' social and environmental impacts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Autumn wreaths and 'doorscaping': Why we need more life in our front gardens
item.description: There was a time when decorative wreaths appeared on front doors in December, stayed on front doors for a few weeks and then disappeared. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Diamond laser system achieves 100% optical contrast in magnetic-field readout
item.description: Researchers at Fraunhofer IAF have developed a laser-enhanced quantum sensor that combines high magnetic-field sensitivity with a large dynamic range. Using laser threshold magnetometry, they improved the ratio of sensitivity and dynamic range by a factor of up to 590 compared with state-of-the-art approaches. The breakthrough is enabled by the first demonstration of 100% optical contrast, combined with strong laser readout signals. The results, published in Nature Communications, open up new prospects for medical diagnostics, navigation, and resource exploration. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Entrepreneurs live longer than salaried workers, study reveals
item.description: Conventional wisdom suggests that the long hours and pressures of entrepreneurship can take a toll on health. But new research by Cristiano Bellavitis, associate professor in the School of Business at Stevens Institute of Technology, and his collaborators finds that entrepreneurs tend to live longer than people who spend their careers working for others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
item.description: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global warming may have halted an emerging ice age, study suggests
item.description: Two thousand years ago, the Arctic remnants of a once-vast ice sheet started to grow again. It was the beginning of a new glacial period, more conversationally known as the next ice age—but by the 1960s, summer temperatures were already so high that the ice sheet started to shrink. In other words, global warming ended a period of glaciation that had already begun. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Earth's hemispheres may have worked together to drive past ice ages
item.description: New research from the University of St Andrews has uncovered a previously unknown process that may have helped drive Earth into past ice ages. Published today (Oct. 22) in the Journal of Climate, the paper links ice sheets in the Northern Hemisphere to changes in ocean circulation and sea ice in the Southern Hemisphere understood to drive down atmospheric CO₂. Linking these two key features of the ice ages has long been a challenge, given how far apart the two regions are. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb captures stars in the early stages of life in a nearby stellar nursery
item.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope continues to reveal hidden parts of the cosmos with its advanced suite of infrared instruments. In a newly released image, Webb revealed many stars previously hidden by the dust clouds of NGC 7129, a stellar nursery about 3,300 light-years from Earth in the constellation Cepheus. The image is already improving our understanding of how new stars are born and evolve with time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb image reveals young stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
item.description: In this Picture of the Month from the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope, we visit a turbulent cauldron of star formation to see what is brewing inside dense clumps of gas. This is a star-forming region named LHA 120-N 159, or simply N159, located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This image spans about 230 light-years across. Publicado también por: European Space Agency. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists turn art detectives to date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual sky from 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's known location and other factors, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon didn't line up. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Mosquito bites are more complicated than they appear—getting a closer look might lead to better disease prevention
item.description: Female mosquitoes need blood to produce eggs. While much research has focused on how these hungry mosquitoes find their targets, less is known about what happens after they land on skin. Yet, a better understanding may allow researchers to find new ways of preventing bites that transmit diseases like malaria and dengue. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When climate data is transformed into visuals, some people and places get overlooked
item.description: When a climate disaster happens, people thousands of miles away may encounter it through numbers: how many people died, how many were displaced, how many homes were destroyed and how much infrastructure was damaged. But for the people living through it, the disaster is not a data set. It is a home, a family, a livelihood and a place. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hay una buena razón por la que Elon Musk quiere juntar Tesla y SpaceX en una empresa de 3,5 billones de dólares: mas control
item.description: El martes, durante la conferencia de resultados de SpaceX , Elon Musk confirmaba que ambas empresas han formado comités especiales para estudiar una fusión. Esta idea de unir SpaceX y Tesla lleva un tiempo pululando y tras la unión entre la firma espacial de Musk y xAI , es un paso que al magnate le interesa especialmente. La empresa combinada tendría un valor de unos 3,5 billones de dólares a los valores actuales de mercado, según cuenta el New York Times, y sería la mayor operación corporativa de la historia en términos económicos. De momento no se ha acordado nada, pero el tema está desde… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Vallejo

item.title: Drought shifts more plant root cells into newly discovered environmental response mode
item.description: Scientists have discovered a hidden layer of identity in plant root cells: an "environmental mode" that switches on in some cells and becomes more common when water is scarce. The study, led by Dr. Marina Oliva and professor Ryan Lister, from the ARC Center of Excellence in Plants for Space and The University of Western Australia's School of Molecular Sciences, examined how plant cells responded to drought conditions. The work is published in Nature Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How does fake tan work, and why does it sometimes smell 'cookie-like'?
item.description: Real tans come from UV-triggered pigment production in living skin; that same UV exposure increases the risk of skin cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: This group may be small, but McNeil River Falls is home to one of the largest seasonal congregations of bears on Earth, with as many as 80 being spotted at once
item.description: This group may be small, but McNeil River Falls is home to one of the largest seasonal congregations of bears on Earth, with as many as 80 being spotted at once Great picture Ver más comentarios Naveen Chilakapati Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: NASA’s Hubble Charts Path for Roman with Gravitational Lenses
item.description: This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Are you using AI to study? Here's how to do it well
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) means high school and college students now have access to a resource that can potentially "do all the work for them." While this can reduce students' immediate stress about submitting assignments, it may negatively impact their long-term learning. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Supermassive black holes ejected from galactic centers? Quasar survey supports decade-old prediction
item.description: By analyzing data on around 100,000 quasars, or extremely luminous galactic nuclei, researchers at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) have found statistical evidence that some supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies are ejected from their positions after forming. The relationship now identified in the data was predicted 10 years ago by members of the same research group, Peter Raffai and Zsolt Frei, together with Zoltán Haiman. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The same novel can spark very different inner worlds in readers
item.description: Every storybook opens a window for our imagination to be freed from the reality of the world around us and escape into the fictional world. While the author's words act as a guide, everyone experiences fiction in their own way, creating vivid mental pictures and even forming an emotional connection with the characters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tire-derived pollutant found at elevated levels in critical fish habitats
item.description: Endangered coho salmon and steelhead trout live and spawn in habitats surrounded by human activity, such as the San Francisco Bay Area. During a recent storm, researchers found high levels of the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone in roadway outflows, creeks and rivers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A SpaceX no le gusta que China le pise los talones, así que va a hacer lo que nadie ha hecho: recuperar y reutilizar las dos etapas de un cohete
item.description: Parece que a Elon Musk no le gusta sentir que alguien le pisa los talones. Hace tiempo que la compañía china Deep Blue Aerospace publicó su interés en recuperar un cohete mediante un sistema de torre con palillos, como Mechazilla. Ahora, además, ha anunciado que las primeras piezas del cohete están saliendo de la cadena de montaje y que todo va viento en popa. Ha sido el momento ideal para que SpaceX anuncie que intentará algo aún más difícil que lo que ya hizo en Mechazilla: recuperar las dos etapas de su cohete Starship mediante ese sistema. Hasta ahora, ni SpaceX ni ninguna otra compañía… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Research tackling immature fruit drop in avocado trees
item.description: Only a percentage of avocados ever make it to harvest, but CSIRO research is working on ways to combat what is called immature fruit abscission or early fruit drop, a major challenge faced by growers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: World-first basic income trial boosts Indigenous livelihoods and Amazon rainforest protection
item.description: A pilot project in which Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon were given an unconditional basic income significantly improved community well-being, strengthened food security and supported rainforest protection, according to analysis by the University of Bath released today. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How much control do we have over picking up an accent? A lot, study finds
item.description: Have you ever binge-watched Bluey or a British crime drama and caught yourself imitating the characters' accents out loud? Rest assured, you are not alone. While it's a common belief that picking up someone else's accent just happens automatically, new research from The Ohio State University suggests that people actually have considerable control over when they adopt or suppress someone else's accent. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Black hole observations uncover evidence of solar storm–like magnetic eruptions
item.description: Technion researchers have presented evidence for the existence of solar-storm-like outbursts near supermassive black holes, which can be a million times larger than the sun or more. The phenomenon was discovered in the vicinity of the black hole in the galaxy NGC 3783, and the researchers' findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fear of giving too little can stop people from giving at all
item.description: We've all done it: convinced ourselves that if we can't donate enough money to a cause, it's better not to give at all. But new research led by Jean Zhang, now a postdoctoral researcher at the Wharton School, suggests we're setting the bar for generosity far too high. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gut bacteria use food cues to help time nutrient absorption, study finds
item.description: Biological clocks are often associated with light. Historically, most people started their days when the sun was up and ended their days when the sun set. But new research from Carnegie Mellon University suggests that some of the body's most important timekeepers live in the gut. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study traces van Gogh's famed 'Starry Night' to an actual night sky from 1889
item.description: Scientists doubling as art detectives have traced Vincent van Gogh's "The Starry Night" to a celestial scene that suggests a new date for one of the world's most famous paintings. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: There should be black holes in our neighborhood. Can we find them?
item.description: Scientific estimates show that there should be between about 100 million and 1 billion stellar-mass black holes in the Milky Way. But they aren't easy to locate. They're not like supermassive black holes (SMBH) at the centers of galaxies. Those are usually easy to spot for different reasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Curtain-like plasma structures explain solar jets' apparent spinning in simulations
item.description: An international team of scientists from the University of Sheffield and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, led by a postdoctoral research fellow from the University of Newcastle, Australia, has discovered that solar jets called spicules, which are 6–8 Mm long, take the form of warped, denser plasma sheets like pleated drapery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drone measurements reveal rapid early growth in eastern Australian humpback whales
item.description: Eastern Australian humpback whales reach nearly their full adult size quickly, a new Griffith University–led study has found, as shown by the first contemporary growth curves for this recovering whale population. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Young women can improve their online experience without giving up social media
item.description: Young women are often exposed to social media content that can contribute to negative body image, but new research has found small, deliberate changes to their feeds could help reduce body image pressures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 350th ESA Council: Media information session
item.description: Video: 01:45:34 Watch the replay of the media information session where ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher and ESA Council Chair at delegate level Juan Carlos Cortés outline the key decisions and main outcomes of the 350th Council meeting held at ESA Headquarters in Paris on 21—22 October 2026. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: En 2023, veinte camiones cruzaron Países Bajos cargados con 400 toneladas de marisma frisia. Su destino era un canal capaz de fabricar tormentas
item.description: Es septiembre de 2023 y estamos en una reserva natural en la costa de Frisia. Hay varias excavadoras clavando en el suelo moldes de acero de dos metros por dos metros. Es, salvando las distancias, lo que Pim Willemsen, investigador de Wageningen y Deltares , llamaba un "cortador de galletas gigante" . El único problema es que cada galleta pesaba entre tres y seis toneladas . Esta es la historia de cómo unos investigadores neerlandeses trasladaron 66 de esas "galletas" en unos 20 camiones y las llevaron hasta Delft para meterlas en un canal de olas. ¿El motivo? Demostrar que esa marisma frisia… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Javier Jiménez

item.title: Legal encounters may offer overlooked opportunities for suicide prevention, analysis suggests
item.description: Picture a forlorn man walking into a lawyer's office after his marriage has collapsed. The bank is threatening foreclosure, and his finances are in tatters. His problems may be legal on paper, but in person they can look far more complicated: panic, shame or the numb resignation of someone who can no longer imagine a way out. He did not come for counseling, and his lawyer is not a therapist. Still, the attorney may be sitting beside him at the worst moment of his life—with a chance to help before despair slides into tragedy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Raised brows and a slow blink make speakers look more confident
item.description: Researchers studying facial movements have found that it's not just what you say, but what your face does when you say it, that counts when it comes to appearing confident when answering a question. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Amid cost‑of‑living worries and concern for the nation's future, stress is reshaping Americans' lives
item.description: U.S. adults appear increasingly likely to view stress as an unavoidable part of daily life, according to the 2026 Stress in America survey by the American Psychological Association. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Schrödinger's penguin: One species, two contrasting outcomes
item.description: A new University of Otago—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka study reveals two vastly different life courses for one of Aotearoa New Zealand's least-studied penguin species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Implicit language hierarchies in English-taught programs create ambivalent positions for multilingual students
item.description: A new study by Miki Shibata, a professor at Hiroshima University's Graduate School of Humanities and Social Sciences, reveals a paradox in Japan's English-medium higher education: Official English instruction coexists with local peer expectations that drive classroom interactions back into Japanese. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds NYC tenant right-to-counsel program linked to fewer ED visits in high-risk neighborhoods
item.description: Residential evictions are associated with adverse health outcomes, particularly among low-income populations. Less is known, however, about whether interventions designed to prevent evictions can improve health outcomes—including whether they may reduce visits to the emergency department (ED). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lost Schrödinger manuscript reveals his true view of quantum randomness
item.description: Unlike classical physics, quantum mechanics generally cannot tell us exactly what will happen in an individual event. Instead, it predicts the probabilities of different outcomes. As one of the theory's early pioneers, Erwin Schrödinger played a key role in debates about what this randomness really means. However, part of his contribution has stayed hidden for more than 80 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
item.description: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Some fish might thrive in a warming climate
item.description: Adelaide University researchers have found that some estuarine fishes that live in habitats with highly variable temperatures can withstand the warmer ocean conditions expected to result from climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tokyo's streets reveal hidden gaps in urban inclusion and quality
item.description: Citywide measures of urban sustainability can conceal sharp differences between neighborhoods. A city may appear to provide good streets overall while some areas lack greenery, openness or pedestrian-friendly space where diverse populations live. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christina Koch, astronauta del Artemis, a días de recibir el Premio Princesa de Asturias: “Espero que aprendamos que es importante conservar y amar el planeta en que nos encontramos”
item.description: Lo dijo la nueva subdirectora de la NASA, en el marco de una conferencia de prensa en Oviedo, donde recibirá la distinción este viernes; se trata de la única mujer que participó de la histórica misión a la Luna Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.
